subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and should the public API be a nested `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` or per-agent policy instead of the requested top-level `allowPrivateNetwork` key?
rationale: The implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes a core SSRF trust boundary and the issue discussion already shows the first simple top-level shape needs maintainer/security judgment before landing.

options.title: Adopt nested audited policy
options.body: Expose a deliberately named nested SSRF policy, preferably scoped per agent, with audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and private-network/redirect/metadata tests.

options.title: Keep arbitrary web_fetch strict
options.body: Reject broad private-network access for `web_fetch` and steer users to trusted proxies, narrow fake-IP flags, or separate tools for internal services.

options.title: Add a simple global toggle
options.body: Accept the larger blast radius of a global broad opt-in and document that operators own the private-network risk.

recommendation.title: Adopt nested audited policy
recommendation.body: Expose a deliberately named nested SSRF policy, preferably scoped per agent, with audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and private-network/redirect/metadata tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest visible issue-thread security decision signal and related SSRF hardening history.
